other_changed_families.note: The IMAP fixture now answers literal continuations generically, so fdm logs in, selects INBOX, fetches and delivers the fixture message over verified IMAPS. The negative CA run reaches the listener but the current run reuses a stopped fixture port (Connection refused), so the wrong-CA abort is not yet asserted; the row is recorded at L6, not promoted.

Diagnosis narrowed: the rfc2818 source path is a poke (Content-Length: 0) plus an authenticated source; the fixture answers both, but the client waits on the challenge connection and never sends the body before the socket timeout. No level change; the payload assertion was not weakened.

The workload is unchanged: Net::DNS::SEC rejects the embedded BIND private key before signing. The fixture needs a module-shipped key pair rather than the hand-written blob; not asserted as a subject result.

The added bounded single read lets the IRC greeting be read without waiting for EOF. The authority then completes the verified TLS greeting; the candidate server fails the same handshake with SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE. This is a candidate-only runtime divergence.

The recipe builds BIND's libisc under the authority but the candidate configure/build stops at libisc_la-error.lo. Both are below L4, so no runtime row exists; the build-level asymmetry is recorded, not promoted to an implementation claim.
